item.title: Flexible GraphRAG v0.11.0 Release Introduces New Desktop App and State Options
item.description:
Flexible GraphRAG v0.11.0 Release Introduces New Desktop App and State Options

The v0.11.0 release introduces an early version of a Desktop App built with Tauri and Rust alongside various backend and architectural updates.

🚀 Availability

  • New v0.11.0 release on 11/16/26.
  • Includes an early version of a Desktop App (Tauri/Rust) around the React, Vue, or Angular UI with 5 Flexible GraphRAG tabs.
  • Adds browsing, ingesting, searching, and graph viewing (5th tab) of local files and folders with auto-sync support.

⚙️ Key details

  • The backend is written in Python, utilizing LlamaIndex and LangChain as peer frameworks.
  • LlamaIndex serves as the default for each pipeline stage, while LangChain can be selected per stage via environment configuration.
  • The API is built as a REST FastAPI service.
  • Frontend options include Angular, React, and Vue TypeScript frontends, alongside an included MCP server.
  • An optional lighter Docker-free configuration uses SQLite as the auto-sync incremental update state store (INCREMENTAL_STATE_STORE=sqlite) along with embedded stores such as LanceDB, BM25, and LadybugDB.
  • Databases and dashboards can be enabled using the provided Docker Compose layout.

🧩 Capabilities and Integrations

  • Supports 14 data sources (10 with incremental auto-sync).
  • Supports 15 property graph databases, 4 RDF triple stores, 10 vector databases, OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, BM25 search, Alfresco, and Nuxeo.
  • File and folder browser available via Browse… in the Alfresco, Nuxeo, CMIS, SharePoint, OneDrive, Box, S3, Azure Blob, GCS, and Google Drive data source forms for both desktop and web UIs.
  • Optional ingest pipeline, hybrid search, and AI query can run through customizable Langflow visual flows utilizing 12 custom Langflow components.
  • Optional ingest can run on a CocoIndex (Rust engine) pipeline reusing the same sources, targets, parsers, and KG extractors, adding step-level memoization and automatic delete reconciliation.
  • Optional integration with Hyland OpenArch as a search and vector store, as well as a store for data sources and document state.

#GraphRAG #Python #Tauri #LlamaIndex #FastAPI

Source: stevereiner/flexible-graphrag

item.title: Memgraph powers real-time GraphRAG with in-memory C++ graph engine and hybrid vector search
item.description:
Memgraph powers real-time GraphRAG with in-memory C++ graph engine and hybrid vector search

Memgraph is a high-performance, in-memory graph database that powers real-time AI context and graph analytics. Built in C/C++, it serves as the graph engine for GraphRAG pipelines, AI memory systems, and agentic workflows. It delivers sub-millisecond multi-hop traversals for any system that needs structured, connected context alongside semantic vector or text search. Memgraph provides both in a single query layer: built-in text and vector indexes for similarity search combined with full graph traversal.

🧩 How it works

The same architecture drives real-time graph analytics for fraud detection, network analysis, infrastructure monitoring, and other operational workloads where performance matters. Memgraph is fully compatible with Neo4j’s Cypher query language, ACID-compliant, and highly available. Built-in vector indexes power hybrid graph retrieval with similarity search in a single query, alongside text and geospatial indexes for keyword and location-aware queries.

⚙️ Key details

The MAGE algorithm library includes 40+ graph algorithms in C++, Python, and CUDA including PageRank, community detection, GNN-based link prediction, temporal graph networks, embeddings, and native ML. Atomic GraphRAG enables pivot search, graph expansion, ranking, and prompt assembly expressed as a single Cypher query. The LLM utility module provides graph-aware context formatting for large language models. The AI Toolkit includes integrations with popular agentic frameworks, MCP server, and ready-made components for building GraphRAG, AI memory, and agent workflows on top of Memgraph.

Real-time schema introspection: SHOW SCHEMA INFO returns the full graph ontology for Text2Cypher and AI agent integration. In-memory C/C++ engine provides sub-millisecond traversals with benchmarked performance. Deep-path traversals support accumulators and path filtering without additional application logic. Custom query modules can be extended with Python, Rust, and C/C++ code natively. Parallel query execution enables concurrent query processing for high-throughput workloads.

🚀 Availability

Native Parquet & JSONL loading allows data to be loaded directly from Parquet and JSONL files on local disk, S3, or HTTP endpoints. Streaming support ingests from Kafka, Pulsar, and RedPanda with dynamic graph algorithms that react to changes in real time. High availability is achieved through Raft-based coordination with automatic failover. Multi-tenancy provides isolated databases with per-tenant role assignments. Fine-grained access control offers role-based and label-based permissions at the node and edge level. Authentication & authorization supports SSO integration, user impersonation, and 30+ granular permissions. Memgraph is licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (APL), Business Source License 1.1.1 (BSL), and MIT Electric License (MEL). Memgraph GitHub repository is available at github.com/memgraph/memgraph. Documentation is hosted at memgraph.com/docs/. Discord community is available at memgr.ph/join-discord. Daily builds can be accessed at memgraph.github.io/daily-builds/. Docker is required to run Memgraph with one command. Memgraph starts with Memgraph Lab when installed via Docker.

#GraphRAG #GraphDatabase #AIMemory #Cypher #VectorSearch #GraphAnalytics

Source: memgraph/memgraph

item.title: LEGO Framework Combines Legal Expert GraphRAG and Expert Chain-of-Thought
item.description:
LEGO Framework Combines Legal Expert GraphRAG and Expert Chain-of-Thought

Researchers have introduced LEGO, a dual-module framework designed to improve complex legal reasoning by synergizing Legal Expert GraphRAG and expert Chain-of-thought.

🧩 How it works

LEGO utilizes two primary modules to handle legal data:

  • ExpertGraphRAG: Employs a greedy normative-coverage retrieval algorithm and an expert-annotated civil code graph of normative relations to dynamically extract instance-specific provision subgraphs.
  • ExpertCoT: Organizes case facts and retrieved provisions into a structured Provision-Fact-Conclusion reasoning format.

⚙️ Key details

Using a Qwen3-8B backbone, the framework demonstrated the following performance metrics:

  • Accuracy: Achieved 40.53% exact-match accuracy on LawExamQA_Civil.
  • Comparative Performance: Outperformed evaluated RAG and CoT baselines and performed comparably to larger evaluated models.
  • Robustness: Maintained robustness on multi-hop questions and achieved the best results among evaluated baselines on open-ended benchmarks.

#LegalAI #GraphRAG #LLM #LegalReasoning

item.title: Unified Knowledge Graph RAG Stack Brings GraphRAG and LightRAG to AWS
item.description:
Unified Knowledge Graph RAG Stack Brings GraphRAG and LightRAG to AWS

A new open-source project named unified-kg-rag-on-aws (licensed under Apache-2.0) integrates two distinct knowledge-graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methodologies—Microsoft’s GraphRAG and HKUDS’s LightRAG—onto a single shared stack. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon OpenSearch Service, this implementation allows users to choose their retrieval methodology per query while sharing the underlying ingestion, indexing, caching, and multilingual handling layers.

🔍 Overview

Knowledge-graph RAG is built to reason over the structured connections within a document corpus. It first turns a corpus into a graph of entities and relationships, then reasons over that structure.

In contrast, standard vector-only RAG retrieves chunks by embedding similarity, meaning it judges each chunk in isolation. While vector-only RAG shines when an answer sits in a single passage that can be found by similarity, its top-k nearest-neighbor retrieval returns locally similar text rather than the connective structures required to answer broader questions.

This project features clean-room re-implementations of both methodologies directly from their respective papers. No upstream code was copied, and all attribution is documented in the project’s THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.

🧩 How it works

Methodology Core Bet Indexing Process Retrieval Process
Microsoft GraphRAG (arXiv:2404.16130) Spend expensive reasoning once at indexing time to keep queries cheap. An LLM extracts an entity-and-relationship graph from the corpus. Leiden community detection then identifies “communities” (clumps of entities referencing each other far more than anything else). An LLM writes summaries of each community and parent clusters, producing a tree of thematic summaries. Global questions fan out across community summaries, gather answers, and map-reduce them into one response (never touching raw documents). Local questions start from named entities and walk outward along their relationships to collect neighbors and text.
HKUDS LightRAG (arXiv:2410.05779) Keep indexing cheap and do the thinking when the question arrives. Extracts an entity-and-relationship graph but stops there, performing no community detection or community summarization. Extracts two kinds of keywords from the query. Low-level keywords (concrete things) are matched against entity descriptions (“what things are” layer). High-level keywords (abstract concepts) are matched against relationship descriptions (“how things connect” layer).

⚙️ Key Details

This project exposes GraphRAG through multiple query execution strategies:

  • Simple: One of the core exposed retrieval strategies.
  • Local: Starts from the entities named in the question and walks outward along their relationships to collect neighboring nodes and text.
  • Global: Fans out across community summaries to perform map-reduce over topics.
  • Drift: One of the core exposed retrieval strategies.
  • Auto: Employs an LLM router to dynamically select the optimal strategy per query.

#RAG #AWS #KnowledgeGraph #GraphRAG #LightRAG

Source: Unified Knowledge Graph RAG on AWS: GraphRAG and LightRAG on one stack | Amazon Web Services
